title: Is EVE Online On It's Last Limb?

posts.cooked:
This entry is intended not as a negative critique, or even a putdown, but as a wake-up call -- a word of advice for not only CCP but EVE Online in general.

I have been involved with EVE Online for almost ten years now. I created my first character on July 9, 2006 at 3:04 Tranquility time. I've witnessed the rise and fall of Band of Brothers. I was present during the battle of FAT-6P. I there at the invasion of Deklein on Krall Amarr's watch while Razor and NC swarmed in unimpeded. I was there when Suddenly Ninja's came into being long before James 315 was ever borne into existence.

I've seen a lot of things happen with EVE Online over the years. I've seen CCP do some pretty innovative things with the game – things no other developer had ever done or would even dare to try but they also made some very poor choices that ended up costing them a great deal as well. Some pretty bad calls were made, Incarna was most likely one of the worst ones CCP had ever made. After a while the CSM was formed by CCP in effort to amend those mistakes in hopes to reverse the direction of the game. Ultimately this failed to reverse the decline of the game and here we are now -- today.

There was a time when Hi-sec was packed with mission runners and miners around the clock. A time when unsuspecting prey still could be found wandering around low-sec that were fat and ripe for the picking. You can find systems that were once bustling with activity reduced down to a faint buzz. Some parts of null have even reached a new level of quiet where you can easily spend 3-4+ hour stretches without seeing so much as a soul pass through.

What happened to EVE Online?

Tranquility is lucky to get near 30,000 logins at one time these days and more than half of those logins are alts, GUARANTEED. Has EVE Online devolved to the point where bitter vets and griefers are most, if not all, that is left of the player base? Has CCP been put into a precarious situation here they are now at the mercy of a small, obsessed community of competitive gamers that is insatiable beyond reason and only plays so they can be spoiled and gratified with the illusion of power and control over other players?

Is the biggest problem in EVE perhaps not so much CCP, but ourselves? Has the EVE Online community been so self serving and spoiled to the point where we have elected to hold CCP at gunpoint in everything they do?

The biggest problem with having a niche MMO, especially ones as expensive and giant as EVE, is that while that niche does not change, the rest of the world does change. EVE Online cannot sustain itself off a aging community comprised of either college graduates who are growing out of the game, intellectuals, nerds, geeks, retired hippies, fat hairy men soaked in alcohol, cannabis enthusiasts and social outcasts.

If EVE Online finally fades away into obscurity it will be for three reasons: CCP's shortsightedness in terms of their plans for not just EVE, but the whole company in itself, and their enabling the the vocal minority of the community and the CSM to influence development policy in the way it has been allowed to as long as it has. Above all else is CCP's dependence on the veteran player-base.

One of the biggest constants in online games is that the success and longevity of a game largely depends on the developers ability to perceive what is going on with the audience and knowing when/how to respond to it. CCP failed to do this before and they created the CSM as a form of damage control and the CEO himself even public apologized to the players. The problem with involving gamers into the development process is that more often than not the gamers don't even know what they really want a lot of the time, only what they want in that moment of time. All that is compounded by the lack of knowing how a particular change or addition can affect everything else down the road for the game. It's almost like consulting your five year old on parental advice -- call it progressive, but it just doesn't work as well as you'd think and sometimes progressive can end up turning out to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

Don't get me wrong – while I do believe that a community involvement in the game development is a innovative way to do things and has a lot of promise... it still has a long ways to go. CCP is not in a position to be able to afford to experiment with the concept. While they have already committed to the idea for as long as they have they cannot just simply back out of the CSM and take it away from the community as the backlash would be rather bad – but things remain what they are, mistakes remain mistakes -- but have we really learned anything yet? What are we supposed to do now?

If EVE Online is to survive it has adapt, it needs to evolve. EVE is going to have to find a way to find a new generation of players and build upon that if it is going to keep going. If CCP has done anything at all that does make sense it is changes they have been trying to make to get new players into the game and make it less daunting to learn how to play. But even still -- this is only one of many steps that CCP is going to have to take to make it all work.

Part of the battle is accumulating new players. That is the easy part – retaining new players is the part that is hard and this is something EVE does not have a very good track record with. Introducing skill injectors is a good step in the right direction to help with this I believe but it is still going to take more than that to make a difference. The problem is I do not believe CCP will do what it takes to make that difference -- not at this time...

The biggest challenge that falls before CCP is wither they are willing to tell the veteran players "no" when the times comes for it. Right now the existing community has CCP by the balls, and they know it – and CCP knows it too, but its killing the game. This has to change if EVE is going to endure and I say this as someone who has been playing for almost 10 years now. It's just the unpopular but undeniable truth and the community has to wake up to it or they won't have a game to play anymore. Either that or go F2P and I don't believe that the F2P model is even compatible with EVE, particularly its complex economy, at all, and it could likely finish EVE Online off for good.

And lets say even if vets and griefers did manage to drive all if not most competition out of the game, noobs and bears alike – what's left after that? What's left for all of EVE? Are you going to cannibalize, or get bored and abandon EVE and CCP after its all said and done and go infect Star Citizen instead? This is a one-way street, and there is nothing at the end. We can either realise what is going on and try to learn from mistakes... or deny what has happened with EVE and let it die within the next 2-4 years. Let the flaming begin!

In short I'm gonna answer like I always do in these sort of threads: Look up on how MMO games in general are failing. WoW which have been around for quite a while have lost more then half of their playerbase, most other MMO:s simply fail completely and fall into obscurity.

I think the main problem for EVE (and MMO:s in general) is that todays players are demanding instant gratification and that'sa why FPS, MOBA and to a lesser extent RTS games are dominating while most other genres are having problems.

In short: Is EVE having problems ... yes ofcourse. However it's more of a general MMO: problem then a specific EVE problem in my eyes. Also note that all 'bad decisions' that CCP have made during the years have been moving away from the core concept of EVE, you claim they listened to much on the 'veterans' when numbers say the problem was more that opposite.
Thought about making a serious response. Then after reading the whole thing...Nah, not worth it. OP's a thinly-veiled carebear rant. That, or trollbait (8/10 if so).

So what you're saying is you want this to become WoW in space? Also I am pretty sure it isn't the griefers/bitter vets who have CCP's ear but rather the carebears, you can thank them for the position we're in right now.

Eh, if anything's taking numbers from EVE it's competition from other games that share something in common with EVE. Many space-themed games and sandbox MMOs have been released lately whereas for much of EVE's lifespan there was a dearth of space games and most MMOs were focused around WoW/Everquest-style questing and raiding.
Ah yes, the good old argument that in order to ensure that the game survives for me to keep playing it, I have to stop playing it for the reasons that draw me to it in the first place.

Originally posted by Mechacaseal:

Here's my two penneth!

I have also been playing EVE for almost 10 years and seen the various iterations over that time. Some of them were good, really good and some of them were atrocious. On the whole, EVE has improved with age.

I have steadily watched the simultaneous playerbase diminish from around 60,000 to a paltry 30,000 during that time and if, as Hijal says, over half of them are now alts, that is a pretty sad indictment of the game as a whole.

The game still gives me the main things that interest me, exploration, PvP, empire building and the questing. However, it still has one major flaw in the gameplay, that has annoyed me, throughout. You can't actually fly the ships, especially the smaller ones, as a true pilot would. Point and click flying or using autopilot is just one step removed from being an RTS.

Now, if CCP really want to add something to the game that will draw in new players, maybe they should consider merging the UI experience from Valkyrie into EVE and give the capsuleers the true pilot experience.

You may all disagree with this, but when you consider that the graddaddy of all these space trading games, Elite was brought bang up to date in Elite Dangerous with online multiplayer capabilities, CCP need to do something to stay current with EVE.

I realise that EVE, Valkyrie and Dust 514 are all set in the same universe in the same timeframe. Maybe it's about time that CCP acknowledged this in more than just the backend server data and unified the user experience into one client, as well. There were rumours a few years ago that you would be able to land on planets and embark on ground adventures, as well. The broad data exists for this as it is used in DUST, so why not merge the front ends, too?

Of the three games currently in CCPs stable, I have played DUST and EVE. Valkyrie is the only one that remains elusive to me, at the moment.

In summary, as a game framework, EVE Online is second to none. It has everything, a rich ecosystem of solar systems, a mature economy, expansive tech tree, hugely varied ships and equipment, trading opportunities and agents to dish out missions of varying complexity.

As a game, it is good but a little lacking in some areas. The flight model and specifically the flight UI is a little anachronistic. Point and click as opposed to roll/pitch/yaw/throttle in flight is counter-intuitive for anyone who has ever used flight or space flight sims.

The time taken to train up necessary skills for noobs can be daunting. I can remember it took me almost 6 months to graduate to a ship that could carry any drones. The injectors go a long way toward alleviating this problem, but the cost is prohibitive, especially as this is on top of the monthly fee.

The CSM is, I fee, too powerful in dictating the direction of the game. If CCP wish to get input from the playerbase, do it in the way that other games do it, by contributions to forums. After all, politicians can't alter the laws of physics with the wave of a wand, so why should a few players be able to do similar to what is fundamentally the "laws of physics" in the EVE universe.

Discuss!

RE: manual fight

There's a reason why EVE has the control scheme that it does. Unlike Elite and all of its clones, the weapons on EVE's ships don't point forward from the nose, and you don't need to point it at the enemy to get a missile lock or whatever. The way EVE handles combat is like a computer-controlled system would, and that is by far more efficient than flying and aiming manually.

You really want manual flying and shooting? Fine. I hope they give it to you. Then you can be like that one drooly-mouthed player who insists on using a controller while playing PC FPS games, while everyone else is a keyboard-and-mouse user. Would make my job easier since I'd know exactly who to go after before anyone else for the easy kill.

Just pure conjecture punctuated with claims of "cold, hard truth" from some Provibear whose idea of playing EVE is watching time-compressed pvp footage set to Evanescence songs while mining in between system lockdowns due to neutral shuttles passing through the region.

I'd like to say that this is somehow new, or that I'm impressed, but the truth is that every two or three months, some "vet" comes though and claims that his age and vast experience in pvp and piracy (lol) qualifies him to make the claim that CCP should make high-sec mission-running just a little bit more safer.

Yawn.
